rationale: Both use the same sound approach: a memoised search over sorted per-title counts that tries every group of distinct titles. A picks each group with itertools.combinations, which is more Pythonic and readable than B's bitmask with mask >> i & 1 and bin(mask).count('1'). A also skips impossible groups by construction instead of generating and discarding them. However, A tracks the minimum with a manual loop and recomputes the group price inline. B precomputes a _GROUP_COST table, uses min(), and has a module docstring plus a function docstring explaining why the sorted tuple is a canonical state. B's padding of the counts to five is a little awkward. Each is clearer in different places, so neither is clearly better.
